thread:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a short burst sweep in staging around the new /v1/generate route and hit 503s once we pushed to ~2.5k RPM from a single API key. not sure if it's quota exhaustion or a routing fallback. logs show 'rate_limiter.reject' and a flurry of 504s from the inference pool.

ajay: thanks for flagging. did you use the internal load harness or wrk? can you paste the exact command + headers you used? also which model variant and shard config?

maria: used our loadtest-bot script (kinda the same as wrk loop) — here's the loop:

```bash
# simplified repro
for i in $(seq 1 1500); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":32}' &
done
wait
```

maria: ran that 3x concurrently (so ~4500 concurrent requests ramping up over ~30s). model: open-llama-13b-8k-qat on 4xA100 pool.

sam: that pattern will absolutely blow through token-bucket bursts if per-key RPM is low. our token bucket is per-api-key with a burst size of 200 tokens (default config) and refill at RPM/60 per second. but the other layer is project/global concurrency limit which will start returning 503s when the pool can't accept more in-flight requests.

kevin: two quick diagnostics: 1) check the "rate_limiter.dispensed_tokens" counter in observability for that api key, 2) check worker queue length on the serving runtime.

maria: attaching the metrics snapshot (copied):

```
rate_limiter.dispensed_tokens{key="team-x"} 184000
rate_limiter.rejects{key="team-x"} 120
serving.runtime.in_flight{pool="a100-4x"} 102
serving.runtime.queue_depth{pool="a100-4x"} 214
request.latency.p95 480ms
request.errors.503 64
```

maria: also noticed billing side weirdness — the tenant saw a sudden jump in billed tokens (we think from retries). unclear if retries were client-side or our automatic retries.

ajay: retries will inflate billed tokens for sure. one of our mitigations is to short-circuit deterministic client retries with 429s instead of 500/503 where applicable, so clients back off instead of hammering. do we have retry headers set in the load harness?

maria: harness had no special Retry-After handling — the loop just kept firing.

loadtest-bot: info — recent load job id=lt-2026-03-12-12-01, avg RPM=2800, peak TPM=164k, max concurrency=1200, duration=90s.

sam: a few notes from the runtime team:
- token-bucket default values are conservative for PLG onboarding but too aggressive for bursty ingestion workloads.
- we have a secondary "burst_pool" that allows short-lived bursts up to N requests for new keys, but it's sized small to prevent abuse.

sam: for this class of test we recommend a two-axis default: per-key RPM default = 1800 RPM, project TPM default = 90k TPM, burst allowance = 600 tokens with a 60s recovery window. those numbers are tuned for our 4xA100 pool characteristics and typical prompt lengths (avg 50 tokens).

kevin: note: those defaults assume no client-side retry amplification. if a client is aggressively retrying on 5xx, effective QPS can be multiple of the intentional traffic. we should document recommended Retry-After behavior in quickstarts.

ajay: can we agree on a benchmark matrix to set "sane defaults"? propose axes:
- concurrency levels (50, 200, 500, 1200)
- sustained RPM targets (100, 600, 1800, 3000)
- burst window durations (5s, 30s, 60s)
- prompt length buckets (short=16, medium=64, long=256 tokens)

ajay: also propose we run two modes: 
1) "friendly" mode (simulate client respects Retry-After and backs off)
2) "hostile" mode (clients retry immediately up to 3x) — this shows billing and tail failure behavior.

maria: that's good. i'll schedule a 2-hour run in staging with the matrix. question: what should we use as acceptance thresholds? i.e., when do we say this default is ok vs needs lowering?

sam: acceptance rules idea:
- p95 latency < 1s for all short/medium prompts at target RPM
- error rate < 0.5% (503/429) for friendly mode
- for hostile mode, ensure system-level protections kick in (global throttles) before backend OOMs — we prefer 429s over 5xx
- billing inflation factor <= 1.15 (retries + duplicates shouldn't increase billed tokens >15%)

kevin: operational caveat: we sometimes see auth token refresh storms (clients refreshing keys simultaneously) which look like bursts. include a test case that does 1000 key rotations per minute across clients to validate the auth service rate limits.

maria: will add key-rotation test. also found a subtle thing: the token-bucket is applied pre-auth in our stack for performance, so unauthenticated floods get rate-limited but you don't see the API key-level metrics until later — makes debugging harder. we should add a correlation id emitted at the preauth stage.

ajay: agreed, add a short-term: emit preauth-correlation header "x-rl-cid" and log it to request traces. long term we can push auth into the early path if needed.

loadtest-bot: action: scheduled job lt-2026-03-13-08-00 with matrix (concurrency=[50,200,500,1200], rpm=[100,600,1800,3000], burst=[5,30,60], prompts=[16,64,256], modes=[friendly,hostile]).

maria: follow-ups: i'll collect p95/p99, error breakdown (429 vs 503 vs 500), token dispensed per key, and billed tokens with and without retries. will paste results in this thread.

kevin: next ops item: update quickstart docs to recommend client-side backoff and include example Retry-After handling (ex exponential backoff with jitter). also add note about billing risk when implementing naive retries.

ajay: one more perf tip — when setting default RPM/TPM in console, provide a "burst preview" simulator that shows expected tokens consumed during common bursts (e.g., 1k concurrent users hitting signup prompt). UX can show estimated billed tokens and likely error rate.

maria: love that. ok i'll run the sweep tomorrow morning and report numbers. tagging @kevin @ajay @sam for any additional tests to include. :thumbsup:

kevin: thumbs up. if we see systemic 5xxs we should have a canary rollback plan for the rate-limiter config.

sam: noted. i'll prep a config toggle (feature-flagged) so we can flip between old/new defaults without deploys.

maria: thanks all — will report back.
